subject: PD brief 7 – 14 Oct 2026: 43 papers, 3 to dig into

synthesis.intro: Cardiac arrest dominated these 8 days — bystander CPR, AED use, and how long to persist — alongside a useful cluster of trauma and toxicology papers. Watch the bias labels: many of the eye-catching findings this period are hypothesis-generating registry signals, not settled practice.
synthesis.discussion: A stranger doing bystander CPR was associated with better survival than family CPR — what is actually going on in those family-witnessed arrests we attend, and what could we realistically change in the first two minutes on scene?

lessons.text: Bystander CPR by a stranger was associated with better survival than CPR by a family member (17.3% vs 9.6% survival to discharge) — when coaching family members on scene, consider whether fatigue, distress or hesitation is affecting compression quality and swap in or coach early.

AEDs work when someone grabs one — bystander application was associated with survival comparable to EMS-delivered shock — yet application rates sat at just 8.5% of public-area opportunities. A reminder to direct a specific bystander to the nearest AED early in public arrests.

Survivors of long resuscitations did not uniformly do badly: after median 14 minutes to ROSC, 5-year survival (~79%) and return to work (~60%) were similar across time-to-ROSC groups, even though brain injury rose with longer arrests. This supports persisting on extended arrests rather than pre-judging futility.

Only about 60% of paramedic-suspected STEMIs were confirmed at discharge, with a spread of NSTEMI, other cardiac and non-cardiac causes — a reminder when handing over that your field interpretation is the start of a workup, not the diagnosis, and worth framing that way to the patient.

Ice-water and cold-water immersion were the fastest cooling modalities for hyperthermia in a large meta-analysis — a useful talking point forheat-exposure jobs where you can access water quickly, alongside the practical limits of immersion on scene.

deep_dives.topic: Persistence and futility in prolonged arrest
deep_dives.why: Two high-transferability papers this period speak directly to the hardest on-scene question: how long is long enough, and what recovery looks like for those who survive long efforts.
questions: How does the finding that long arrests can still yield working, surviving patients sit with your own futility thresholds on scene?
What would it take before the amiodarone signal (better ROSC and 24-hour survival, but no significant neurological benefit) would change what you reach for after rhythm conversion?
deep_dives.ideas: Compare how the long-resuscitation study defines a good outcome (return to work, nursing-home admission) against what you and your crew consider meaningful survival, and consider whether the amiodarone registry findings would survive randomisation.

deep_dives.topic: Trauma decisions: TXA, binders and bleeding assessment
deep_dives.why: Trauma papers this period cut both ways — a promising prehospital TXA subgroup finding, but sobering evidence that we cannot reliably pick who benefits from a pelvic binder in the field.
questions: The TXA benefit was a subgroup analysed after hospital arrival phenotyping — how much should that shape your confidence in giving TXA now?
If 56% of pelvic injuries may be potentially harmed or unaffected by binder placement, what does that mean for your index of suspicion and technique?
deep_dives.ideas: Compare the TXA subgroup's fibrinolysis phenotyping (done on hospital arrival) with what you can actually assess prehospital, and look at whether the Doppler simulation findings match how you currently confirm tourniquet effectiveness after application.

deep_dives.why: Paediatrics came up repeatedly this period — video laryngoscopy evidence, MAP centiles and paramedics rating themselves lowest in neonatal and paediatric mental health — making it a natural combined PD focus.
questions: Does the small first-pass success advantage for video laryngoscopy (72.2% vs 69.0%, from mostly observational studies) match your experience with the devices available to you?
Where do your own self-rated gaps sit against the survey's lowest scores for paediatric behavioural and mental health emergencies?
How would age-adjusted MAP centiles change your assessment of the sick child beyond standard vital sign ranges?
deep_dives.ideas: Consider how the MAP centile study's finding that 41% of EMS encounters sat above the 95th centile fits with your local guideline's paediatric blood pressure thresholds, and ask whether the self-rated competence gaps in the survey point to simulation topics worth requesting in your service's training calendar.

papers.title: Cancer markedly raises OHCA risk
papers.n: ~800,000 adults with cancer and 3.7 million matched controls
papers.finding: 55% higher hazard of OHCA with cancer (adjusted HR 1.55, 95% CI 1.50–1.60); roughly 6-fold short-term hazard with lung and neurological cancers, strongest within the first year after diagnosis

papers.title: Prehospital RSI: what makes it hard
papers.n: 39 emergency care practitioners
papers.finding: Three themes: system-driven administrative demands and procedural complexity, resource and workforce constraints, and communication-related challenges and information gaps affecting clinical decision-making

papers.title: On-site CT slashes event transports
papers.n: 498 patients imaged on-site
papers.finding: 429 of 498 (86%) discharged on-site after imaging; 52 (10%) required hospital transport; 429 EMS transports and ~22,737 minutes of EMS deployment time avoided versus the pre-CT period

papers.title: EMS dashboards: thin crisis evidence
papers.n: 26 studies
papers.finding: KPIs mapped to the Donabedian structure/process/outcome model with time-based indicators most frequent; 8 of 26 studies (31%) reported dashboards, all in routine operations, and only one study addressed crisis conditions (without a dashboard)

papers.title: Amiodarone after non-shockable-to-shockable conversion
papers.n: 5,535 adults with non-traumatic OHCA (1,843 matched pairs)
papers.finding: Amiodarone was associated with higher admission with ROSC (26.7% vs 23.0%; OR 1.22), 24-hour survival (21.4% vs 14.7%; OR 1.58) and survival to discharge (6.5% vs 4.2%; OR 1.58), but favourable neurological outcome was not statistically significant (3.7% vs 2.9%; OR 1.31, 95% CI 0.91-1.89)

papers.title: Long resuscitations don't rule out good recovery
papers.design: National registry cohort, stratified by time-to-ROSC
papers.n: 2,583 bystander-witnessed OHCA survivors (median age 65, median time-to-ROSC 14 min)
papers.finding: Anoxic brain damage increased with time-to-ROSC (0.3%, 1.8% and 3.2% for 0-10, 11-18 and >18 min; adjusted HR 9.98 for >18 min vs 0-10 min), but 5-year survival (~79%), return to work (~60%) and nursing-home admission did not differ between groups

papers.title: Family CPR helps — but strangers' CPR helps more
papers.design: Retrospective registry cohort (multivariable mixed-effects logistic regression)
papers.n: 824,960 non-traumatic OHCAs, 2013-2024
papers.finding: Survival to discharge was 9.6% with family-member bystander CPR (aOR 1.31 vs none) and 17.3% with non-family bystander CPR (aOR 1.58 vs none); non-family CPR beat family CPR directly (aOR 1.21), with the same pattern for favourable neurological survival

papers.title: Bystander AEDs work — when someone actually grabs one
papers.design: Retrospective multicentre registry analysis with propensity and weighting methods
papers.n: 23,918 adults with presumed medical OHCA (383 bystander AED applications)
papers.finding: Bystander AED application was associated with higher survival (aOR 1.60) and good neurological outcome (aOR 2.31) versus no prehospital defibrillation, comparable to EMS-delivered shock; yet AEDs were applied in only 8.5% of public-area versus 1.9% of non-public opportunity cases

papers.title: Only a third of arrests get bystander CPR
papers.n: 229 studies, 4,421,570 OHCA patients across 45 countries
papers.finding: Pooled bystander CPR prevalence was 32.1% (95% CI 29.7-34.5%), higher in high-income countries (34.9% vs 13.9%) and for paediatric arrests (49.2% vs 31.4%), with residential arrests 28% less likely to receive CPR than public ones (RR 0.72)

papers.title: Age-adjusted MAP centiles for sick kids
papers.design: Retrospective observational study across three datasets (reference centile derivation and validation)
papers.n: 529,475 EMS encounters, 4,221,048 ED encounters and 4,784 critical care transports
papers.finding: Calculated and measured MAP agreed closely (ICC 0.996); only 0.6% of EMS encounters fell below the 5th centile while 41.0% sat above the 95th, lower MAP was associated with increased mortality, vasoactive use and IV fluid use, and 16.9% of neonates in the EMS sample fell below the 5th centile

papers.title: Defibrillation strategy RCT gets underway
papers.n: Planned 909; 320 enrolled by September 2026 (Denmark, Finland, Belgium, Ireland)
papers.finding: Protocol only — adults with shockable OHCA and two manual defibrillators available are randomised 1:1:1 to anterior-lateral, anterior-posterior, or double sequential defibrillation, with 30-day survival as the primary outcome; no efficacy results reported

papers.title: Only 60% of paramedic-suspected STEMI confirmed
papers.n: 7,205 suspected STEMI visits with a recorded discharge diagnosis (of 8,077)
papers.finding: STEMI confirmed in 4,330/7,205 (60.1%); non-ST-elevation ACS or other coronary syndromes 11.4%; other cardiac 10.5%; noncardiac 8.5%; coronary angiography 67.1%, PCI 44.4%; 30-day mortality 6.5% and 17.5% over median 2.8 years follow-up

papers.title: Bystander CPR up but outcomes flat in the very old
papers.design: National registry cohort with temporal trend analysis
papers.n: 322,943 people aged ≥65 with bystander-witnessed cardiac OHCA
papers.finding: Bystander CPR increased significantly in all age and bystander-relationship strata (all p<0.001) but remained ~50% in family-witnessed arrests; CPC 1–2 at 1 month improved only in the 65–74 group with non-family bystanders; in those ≥90 bystander CPR reached ~80% while CPC 1–2 stayed flat at ~1%

papers.title: CPR injuries common after long arrests
papers.n: 136 OHCA patients (of 313 screened)
papers.finding: 58/136 (43%) sustained injuries, 23 (16.9%) clinically significant; CPR >20 minutes associated with injury (OR 2.45, 95% CI 1.15–5.23); mortality higher in injured patients (70% vs 43%)

papers.title: Ice-water immersion wins for drug hyperthermia
papers.n: 71 studies, 1,932 patients, 12 cooling modalities
papers.finding: Ice-water immersion cooled at 0.169 ± 0.027 °C/min and cold-water immersion at 0.162 ± 0.037 °C/min — the fastest modalities; ice-water-soaked sheets/towels 0.121 ± 0.030 °C/min; meta-analysis confirmed immersion beats passive cooling

papers.title: Video laryngoscopy edges out direct in kids
papers.n: 18 studies (17 observational, 1 RCT) in paediatric acute care
papers.finding: First-pass success 72.2% vs 69.0% with direct laryngoscopy (RR 1.11, 95% CI 1.06–1.16); severe intubation-associated events 7.7% vs 11.8% (RR 0.76, 95% CI 0.62–0.93); overall success and desaturation similar; no survival or cardiac arrest data

papers.title: Sepsis intubations: haemodynamic trouble common
papers.design: Retrospective analysis of a prospective multi-centre registry
papers.n: 280 sepsis intubations of 11,289 registry intubations (30 paediatric)
papers.finding: 2.5% of all ED intubations were for sepsis; haemodynamic complications 27.9% and peri-intubation cardiac arrest 4.6%; waveform capnography 87.5% vs 94.1% in non-sepsis (p<0.001); laryngoscopic view and first-pass success comparable to non-sepsis

papers.title: Field fluids before ROSC in crush arrests
papers.journal: Ulusal Travma Ve Acil Cerrahi Dergisi = Turkish Journal of Trauma & Emergency Surgery
papers.n: 37 adults in arrest within 24 hours of the earthquakes
papers.finding: ROSC in 10/37 (27.0%), all of whom had received pre-hospital fluids (mean 1,540 ± 611 mL; p=0.010); fluid recipients had higher pH and lower lactate, potassium, and base excess on arrival

papers.title: 12-lead transmission lags equipment availability
papers.n: 588 of 723 Japanese fire departments (81.3% response)
papers.finding: 545/588 (92.7%) had at least partial recording equipment but only 57 (9.7%) routinely recorded and transmitted; ACS/chest pain protocols (OR 2.89) and routine recording (OR 2.88) predicted transmission adoption; uptake higher where only one PCI-capable hospital existed (46% vs 30%)

papers.title: Little evidence for call handler wellbeing programs
papers.n: 12 studies (n=9 to 4,020 participants)
papers.finding: Interventions fell into four categories — psychoeducation/resilience training, residential recovery, organisational wellbeing initiatives, and multicomponent programs — but there was limited evidence of effectiveness for health, wellbeing, or stress outcomes; most studies assessed mental health only and samples mixed call handlers with first responders

papers.title: ITDs in OHCA: early wins, late losses
papers.n: 97,439 adults with non-traumatic OHCA
papers.finding: ITD-only: ROSC 26.7% vs 23.8% (aOR 1.09) but survival to discharge 23.9% vs 32.0% (aOR 0.68), with worse neurological outcomes; ITD+ACD showed more extreme versions of both trends

papers.title: Paediatric OHCA in Australia and NZ: Aus-ROC report
papers.n: Not reported — abstract not yet available
papers.finding: Not yet available — abstract to come

papers.title: Unwitnessed arrests: mostly women, mostly at home
papers.n: 22 studies, 210,028 adults
papers.finding: Female sex and home location most consistently associated with unwitnessed arrest; limited evidence for arrests at night or during sleep, low socioeconomic status, type I diabetes and psychiatric illness

papers.title: Redirecting non-urgent patients to primary care looks safe
papers.n: 9 studies (8 observational, 1 RCT)
papers.finding: Return rate 9.7%, hospitalisation 1.7%, mortality 0.07%; studies reporting zero hospitalisations and deaths used the richest set of implementation components around triage and documentation

papers.title: Paramedics feel weakest in neonatal and paediatric mental health
papers.n: 253 paramedics
papers.finding: Self-rated competence 2.92 (paediatric) and 2.04 (neonatal); paediatric behavioural and mental health emergencies lowest at 1.30; simulation and clinical placement opportunities limited, especially in neonatal care

papers.title: Building a prehospital suicidal-ideation policy from scratch
papers.n: Single county EMS system; clinician and ED survey samples not reported
papers.finding: Five improvement domains identified: standardised terminology, evidence-based risk assessment, disposition decision support, safety planning protocols, and law-enforcement collaboration; no validated prehospital suicide screening instruments were found

papers.title: Priority transport in multi-patient crashes: sicker, not harmed
papers.design: Nationwide retrospective cohort with doubly robust (AIPW) analysis
papers.n: 143,130 patients from 13.8 million EMS records
papers.finding: Priority transport associated with a 2.2-point adjusted risk difference for death/critical-severe injury (peak 6.4 points at 5-minute scene times, minimum 1.4 points at ~32 minutes), consistent with severity-dependent selection

papers.title: Prehospital TXA helps fibrinolytic shutdown
papers.journal: The Journal of Trauma and Acute Care Surgery
papers.design: Pooled analysis of two prospective prehospital TXA RCTs
papers.n: 1,249 trauma patients
papers.finding: 30-day mortality 14.5% with fibrinolytic shutdown vs 6.5% physiological fibrinolysis; TXA in shutdown patients was associated with lower risk of death (HR 0.32, 95% CI 0.11–0.91); hyperfibrinolysis independently predicted death (HR 2.87, 95% CI 1.10–7.53)

papers.title: Opioid OHCA outcomes similar to other arrests
papers.design: Retrospective registry cohort with toxicological case classification
papers.n: 10,786 EMS-treated OHCA (1,349 opioid-associated)
papers.finding: No association between opioid-associated OHCA and favourable neurological outcome (OR 1.02, 95% CI 0.77–1.35), but significant interactions for sex (p=0.032), initial rhythm (p=0.024) and bystander-witnessed status (p<0.001)

papers.title: Three post-ROSC lab phenotypes predict outcome
papers.design: Retrospective national registry cohort with latent class analysis
papers.n: 1,514 resuscitated adults with presumed cardiac OHCA
papers.finding: Multi-organ dysfunction phenotype had higher odds of poor neurological recovery versus homeostatic (aOR 0.50, 95% CI 0.30–0.78) and immune-dysregulated (aOR 0.46, 95% CI 0.26–0.78) phenotypes, with mortality differences persisting to 3 years

papers.title: Prehospital variables can't pick pelvic binder benefit
papers.design: Retrospective imaging review at a tertiary trauma centre
papers.n: 298 adults with CT-confirmed pelvic ring injury
papers.finding: Binder application would be favourable in only 17% (95% CI 13–22%), neutral in 28% and potentially unfavourable in 56%; the best-performing variable (ISS) reached just AUC 0.65, all others below 0.60

papers.title: Italian HEMS trauma mortality predictors
papers.journal: European Journal of Trauma and Emergency Surgery
papers.n: 3,143 HEMS-managed trauma patients with outcome data
papers.finding: In-hospital mortality 3.4%; independently associated with RTS <4 (OR 5.19, 95% CI 1.64–17.04), RTS 4–<7 (OR 2.36), older age (OR 1.03 per year), tracheal intubation and prehospital CPR

papers.title: Bedside observations beat NEWS for spotting deterioration
papers.design: Retrospective analysis of prospectively collected data on rapid response team arrivals
papers.n: 4,581 adults in general medical, surgical or intermediate care units at a 450-bed US regional centre
papers.finding: Eight equipment-free observations predicted death within 24 hours — jaundice, supplemental oxygen need, capillary refill time, cold skin, distressed breathing, altered mentation, dry skin and cyanosis — and a model of all eight beat NEWS (AUC 0.790 vs 0.707, p < 0.0001)

papers.title: Stable penetrating chest trauma: surgery increasingly avoided
papers.n: 268 haemodynamically stable patients with penetrating chest trauma sparing the cardiac box
papers.finding: Initial non-operative management in 78% of patients; failure rates low and unchanged between periods (8.5% vs 6.5%), with hospital length of stay dropping from 7.6 to 5.2 days after mid-2020

papers.title: Lactate drives prehospital mSOFA risk
papers.n: 12,212 adults transferred at high priority across three Spanish EMS
papers.finding: Cohort mortality was 5.0%; the decision tree's first split was lactate at 3.8 mmol/L, followed by SaFi, GCS and creatinine (order depending on lactate level)

papers.title: Who calls an ambulance for low-acuity problems
papers.design: Retrospective multicentre observational cohort (secondary EHR analysis)
papers.n: 41,761 low-acuity ED encounters across 21 EDs
papers.finding: 3,232 of 41,761 discharged low-acuity patients (7.7%) arrived by EMS; nighttime presentation (aOR 1.63) and mental health diagnosis (aOR 1.76) also raised the odds

papers.title: What makes an ambulance driver competent
papers.n: 19 studies from Europe, Asia, the Middle East and South America
papers.finding: Seven competency domains identified: technical driving; safety and risk management; cognitive and decision-making; communication and teamwork; stress and emotional management; professional and personal attributes; and work ability and fitness

papers.title: Prehospital olanzapine for meth toxicity
papers.design: Retrospective pre-post population-based cohort (inverse probability of treatment weighting)
papers.n: 1,041 individuals with methamphetamine-related contacts, 222 given prehospital olanzapine
papers.finding: Olanzapine recipients more likely to be transported to ED (aOR 11.83, 95% CI 3.19–43.80) and less likely to leave ED without being seen (aOR 0.56, 95% CI 0.32–0.97)

papers.title: Doppler beats pulse check after tourniquet
papers.n: 41 actively practising paramedics, upper-extremity tourniquet application
papers.finding: Pulse palpation sensitivity 66.7%, specificity 87.0%, accuracy 78.0%; paramedic Doppler sensitivity 88.9%, specificity 91.3%, accuracy 90.2%

papers.title: Child visitor injuries in Queensland
papers.design: Retrospective descriptive geospatial analysis of ambulance records
papers.n: 3,802 ambulance attendances, non-Queensland residents ≤15 years, 2009–2018
papers.finding: Interstate visitors 85.8% of cases; falls and transport incidents leading mechanisms; burns third-leading mechanism for interstate visitors aged 0–4; coastal locations most common

papers.title: Two paramedic attitudes to paediatric pain
papers.design: Prospective cross-sectional survey with latent class analysis
papers.n: 129 paramedics
papers.finding: Two profiles: proactive/system-oriented (57.4%, higher endorsement of dosing apps, analgesia algorithms, post-analgesia monitoring and non-pharmacologic adjuncts) vs conservative/low-engagement (42.6%); profile membership not associated with demographics or experience

papers.title: Mechanical vs manual BVM in adult CPR
papers.n: Not reported
papers.finding: Abstract not yet available

papers.title: Community paramedic referrals cut ambulance use
papers.n: 68 program graduates (321 community paramedic visits)
papers.finding: 43% fewer 911 ambulance transports, 46% fewer ED visits and 42% fewer hospital admissions in the six months post-program versus six months before
